qualification_reason: Confirmed meaningful Medical Malpractice service-page gap plus a publicly evidenced direct email for the firm's principal decision maker. The live site explicitly says Tom Fowler Law assists medical-malpractice victims, while the primary practice navigation gives focused pages to other major injury services and does not provide a dedicated Medical Malpractice client page.
campaign_notes: Live-site validation completed 2026-09-04. The primary navigation and homepage were inspected. Dedicated pages exist for Car Accident, Truck Accident, Motorcycle Accident, Bicycle Accident, Pedestrian Accident, Workers' Compensation, Wrongful Death, Slip and Fall, and Dog Bites. The homepage explicitly states the firm can assist when medical malpractice causes serious harm and repeats medical malpractice as an example of work the firm understands. A site-restricted search found medical-malpractice blog/content, including 'Common Mistakes to Avoid when Handling a Medical Malpractice Claim,' but no focused Medical Malpractice service destination in the practice navigation. Medical-malpractice clients have a materially different journey from vehicle-crash and workplace-injury clients. Tom Fowler is the firm's named attorney on the official site; the About page describes Tom Fowler Law as a family-run business with one attorney, and the official Contact page publishes tom@tomfowlerlaw.com.

service_gap_evidence.service_offered_evidence: The official homepage states: 'Whether a car accident led to a fracture or medical malpractice put the victim on the brink of death, we are confident that we can assist,' and separately says that whether it is medical malpractice or a car accident, clients need a trusted Des Moines personal injury attorney. A current firm article also states Tom Fowler Law can help victims of medical errors pursue compensation.

outreach_draft.subject: Your medical malpractice content caught my eye
outreach_draft.body:
Tom,

I noticed your main practice navigation gives car, truck, motorcycle, workers’ comp, wrongful death, slip-and-fall and dog-bite matters their own pages, while Medical Malpractice is something you explicitly say the firm can handle but it still lives inside broader injury content and articles.

That feels like a different client conversation. Someone dealing with a medical error is trying to understand negligence, records, providers and whether they even have a viable case—not the same questions as someone coming in after a crash or workplace injury.

A focused Medical Malpractice page could:
- speak directly to that type of client
- give Google a focused page to crawl and index
- give AI tools clearer context about that part of the firm’s work

You already have useful malpractice content, so I’m using that as the first mockup example.

I’m putting together a quick mockup to show you what I mean. I’ll send it over in the next couple of days.

If you’d rather I didn’t, just let me know.
